text: End me, or free me, the Warden begged. He isn't finished, and only the summons understand him.
Nib translates in a whisper. The pipes are his drip and his drain, both at once.
Then he names the catch.
Nib's voice cracks. Without the pipes he dies within the hour, and when a boss dies, its gate shuts on everyone.
Uncle Pyo stares up toward the rim, far above in the dark.
Then the system weighs in like a broker: forty billion won for his core. No other button.
Rent paid until the sun burns out, and the price is every life in this gate.
He swipes it away without a second look.
He answers honestly, with a head count. End him now, and everyone here dies. Even the men who did this.
The water jumps. Why should the Warden spare the men who put the pipes in him?
Jaeha doesn't look away. Even them. His hyung's rule has no exceptions.
The great eye closes. One long breath, and across the pit, the glass wall fogs white.
When it opens, the anger is gone. Then they must leave him, he says. He's been left before.
Only for now, Jaeha swears. He'll come back for him. Nib's commander once promised the same and never came, so Nib asks: does he say that to everyone? He does.
The eye softens. He has heard that promise before, from someone in orange.
Nib passes it on, and stares at Jaeha. A trap-tester once walked into this gate and never came out.
Jaeha's hand closes on the rusted lamp at his belt. That was his hyung.
Before the machines, Minseok sat at the giant's feet for three days, talking and laughing. The Warden never knew the words, only the smile.
At the end, his hyung had company. And for three days, so did the giant.
Jaeha bows over the lamp and cries without a sound. The promise has two names on it now.
He wipes his eyes. They need proof Kanghan can't wave away, and Moon Ahin already has her phone out.
She turns the camera on her own face, the chained giant behind her. Anyone can call a trap-tester a liar. Not Kanghan's heir.
Then she turns the phone on her family's handiwork.
The tanks, her grandfather's seal on every cap.
The stamped chains. The pipes driven into his coral.
Her eyes shine, but not one tear falls.
Uncle Pyo limps in and pulls off his respirator. Kanghan paid him to be a number. He gives his name instead.
Dami, Woo and Ho bare their faces too. Nobody here is a number anymore.
Jaeha watches them, and his tired face breaks into pride.
She stops the recording. They have their proof.
Troopers come round the pit wall, and the speakers make it plain: to Kanghan, the giant is equipment.
Behind Borro's mask, a green glow kindles. Someone once asked if he was equipment. He corrected them.
Borro says the word back, slowly. Jaeha lets him go. Whatever he does next, Jaeha will carry it.
Borro flares into field form and wraps both hands round a pipe as thick as a tree.
And he rips it out with his bare hands. Violet light geysers across the pit.
Jaeha carries sixty percent of the strain, on his knees in the water, bleeding again.
And for the first time in four years, the Warden breathes easy.
Borro drops the pipe and turns. The slowest voice in the gate speaks for both giants: he is not equipment. Neither am I.
Lyra wipes her eyes, grinning fiercely. The big one keeps going up in her estimation.
In the control room, engineers panic in their only language: yield. One pipe just cost them twelve percent.
The duty chief slams a red button. Kanghan's answer to trouble never changes: shut the door with it inside.
A red countdown. In twelve minutes the rim seals, and with it, the only way out.
Four hundred metres up, the steel frame round the rim starts to close like an iris.
Two hours down, Moon Ahin shouts, and twelve minutes to get out. Jaeha just points at the drain. The sea leaves this way. So can they.
The troopers open fire, and Borro plants himself in front of the hatch, shield up.
The crew and the husks pour through, Nib waving them in.
Jaeha looks back once more. The giant doesn't beg now. He gives an order: go, and come back.
Jaeha answers with a thumbs-up, the way Minseok used to.
The giant eye closes once, slowly. A nod.
Borro backs in last and swings the hatch shut. For once, a closing door is on their side.
Inside, an old tide channel climbs into the dark, black water pumped uphill beside a narrow walkway.
Moon Ahin asks if the video is enough. Only if it gets out. Minseok's spent four years hidden in a shield.
At the rear, Lyra walks backwards, arrow nocked. Below them, the troopers are climbing too.
Far below, a trooper's radio blinks.
The voice on it is Han Sora's. The troopers aren't there to catch them, only to drive them up to her.
Then the whole tunnel shudders, and a crack runs across the ceiling.
Grit patters on Nib's mask. The closing iris is rattling the whole gate, and these tunnels are old.
Eight minutes thirty-one, and a long climb ahead.
And just ahead of them, the ceiling starts to come down.
